source_review.notes: Reviewed the Merkle CRYPTO bibliographic record and author-hosted certified-signature paper, RFC 9162 and RFC 6962, NIST FIPS 180-4 page, official Git object documentation, and official Trillian repository. All seven final destinations returned HTTP 200. Domain-separation, proof, hash, and systems claims remain scoped to the named protocol, assumptions, and trust model.

evidence: Checked H, encode, leaf/internal hash, root, inclusion/non-inclusion/consistency/multiproof, checkpoint, witness, and generation definitions.
Checked byte concatenation, domain tags, ordered children, digest lengths, leaf indices, tree sizes, and shape metadata are distinct and explicit.
Checked collision/second-preimage assumptions are separated from root authenticity, freshness, authorization, availability, and consensus.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The bounded model's complete four-leaf shape is never presented as the chapter's odd-tree protocol.

evidence: Independently recomputed the SHA-256 root 42fc54eeb6352f90cc81fdd5791292cca3974a168208b395b06a76240b24884d.
Recomputed gamma leaf hash, delta sibling hash, alpha/beta parent hash, and the two-step ordered proof.
Recomputed two-level path length for four leaves and verified uppercase GAMMA rejects against the fixed root.
Checked update examples allocate one changed leaf plus log2(n) ancestors for complete power-of-two trees.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Digest inputs use literal bytes 0x00 and 0x01 followed by canonical payload or two 32-byte ordered child digests.

evidence: Derived inclusion correctness by induction from leaf authentication through one ordered sibling per height.
Derived the log2(n) proof length for complete n=2^h binary trees and qualified irregular/sparse variants.
Reviewed the first-differing-node collision/second-preimage security sketch under domain-separated canonical encoding.
Reviewed copy-on-write publication preservation and distinguished it from durability, availability, and reclamation proofs.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The security sketch is explicitly not a construction-specific cryptographic reduction.

evidence: Reviewed empty, singleton, power-of-two, and odd leaf counts under incompatible shape rules.
Reviewed ambiguous encodings, reordered/duplicate leaves, wrong directions/count/index/algorithm/tag/digest length, extra/truncated siblings, and trailing bytes.
Reviewed absence overclaims, consistency-size reversal, multiproof duplicates, old checkpoints, split views, signer/hash rotation, and downgrade.
Reviewed missing nodes, premature publication, crash tails, replica loss, active readers, garbage collection, parser exhaustion, and unavailable content.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable vector excludes odd shapes, empty trees, absence, consistency, multiproofs, signatures, persistence, and hostile parsing.

evidence: Verified every leaf uses 0x00 domain separation and every internal node uses 0x01 with ordered children.
Verified the proof for index 2 supplies the right delta leaf digest then the left alpha/beta subtree digest.
Verified recomputation accepts gamma and rejects changed leaf bytes against the same root.
Verified exact ten-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the safe verifier.
invariant_checking.notes: The expected root is fixture data; the model does not authenticate it through a signature or checkpoint.

evidence: Reviewed inclusion induction against canonical leaf bytes, exact sibling directions, and an authenticated expected root.
Reviewed logarithmic bound against a complete balanced tree rather than claiming it for arbitrary topology.
Reviewed security boundary against collision/second-preimage assumptions and excluded authenticity/freshness/availability conclusions.
Reviewed atomic generation invariant against durable reachable nodes and one checkpoint/root publication boundary.
proof_review.notes: No formal proof is claimed for RFC consistency algorithms, sparse absence, multiproof encoding, signer policy, split-view detection, storage recovery, or hash migration.

evidence: Separated binary list trees, sparse trees, tries, B-trees, DAGs, accumulators, and consensus constructions.
Separated inclusion, absence, range/multiproof, and append-only consistency semantics.
The Python model explicitly disclaims odd counts, application records, signatures, agility, persistence, replication, recovery, and availability.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter uses commitment and authenticated-state language rather than an absolute tamper-proof claim.

evidence: The standard-library hashlib model passed exact expected output under the repository safe snippet runner.
A separate SHA-256 recomputation reproduced leaf, sibling, parent, root, and ordered proof values.
All seven final chapter destinations returned HTTP 200 on the review date.
Local structure, link shape, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet checks passed before review completion.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No independent-language implementation, odd-shape suite, RFC proof generator, sparse map, signature/witness system, fuzzing, cryptographic certification, crash injection, benchmark, or deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter treats Merkle trees as versioned commitment protocols, derives inclusion mechanics, distinguishes proof families and topology variants, and makes authenticated roots and hash assumptions explicit.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed canonical encoding, checkpoint trust/freshness, algorithm migration, immutable node publication, replication/availability, retention and GC, bounded parsing, recovery, witnessing, and split-view response.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review fixes trust and encoding invariants; one exact SHA-256 vector anchors mechanics; ten examples expose protocol and operational failures; five exercises span computation, proof, map design, log operations, and interoperability.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/author/official/bibliographic-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Merkle, IETF, NIST, Git, Trillian, cryptographic, transparency-log, distributed-systems, database, storage, supply-chain, networking, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production authenticated structure, formal cryptographic reduction, RFC implementation, sparse/absence/multiproof/consistency correctness, trusted checkpoint system, hash migration, durable availability, split-view resistance, certification, nor deployment fitness.
